chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Ali (peace be upon him), regarding

the man who comes to the people (combatants), and they had acquired war booty, and he had not been present for the fighting. So Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'They are the deprived ones', and (but still) he ordered that it should be distributed to them.
ai.seo_question: Do soldiers who arrive after the battle receive a share of the war booty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s (as) ruling that those who arrive after the battle has concluded but before the booty is distributed are entitled to their share, emphasizing that mere presence in the camp suffices for inclusion. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the 'ghazw' (campaign) includes the period of consolidation and return, ensuring fairness for all who contributed to the military effort's outcome. It underscores the principle that the reward is tied to the collective success of the army rather than solely to individual combat prowess.

the man who comes to the people (combatants), and they had acquired war booty, and he had not been present for the fighting. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are the deprives ones’, and (but still) he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that it should be distributed to them’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the same narrator (the narrator of the previous Hadith) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from abu ‘Abd Allah from his ancestors, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “About a man

who joins an army who have captured properties but he has not taken part in fighting Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’These people are deprived (from reward). He however, commanded to give such people a share.’”
